classifications.rationale: The President presently determines that Romania’s statutory waiver will expire without renewal at the close of July 2, 1988; the resulting legal consequence occurs upon that expiration, while the report to Congress merely records the action.
classifications.evidence: allow the waiver for Romania under section 402 of the Act (19 U.S.C. 2432) to expire as scheduled at the close of July 2, 1988, without renewal at that time

classifications.rationale: The provision itself prescribes column-2 customs duties for Romanian articles and ends Romania’s eligibility for federal credits and guarantees, effective July 3, 1988; the accompanying statutory-authority statements do not defer those consequences to later agency action.
classifications.evidence: Romania shall no longer be eligible to receive credits or guarantees under any program of the U.S. Government

classifications.rationale: The President directly imposes column-2 duties, modifies the tariff schedule, and terminates Romania’s program eligibility, with those legal effects taking effect July 3, 1988.
classifications.evidence: General Headnote 3(d) to the TSUS, setting forth those countries whose products, whether imported directly or indirectly, shall be dutied at the rates of duty shown in the column numbered 2 of such schedules, is modified by inserting in alphabetical sequence "Socialist Republic of Romania"
